newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares yet again lagging Wall St rise.
newsitem.headline: German shares yet again lagging Wall St rise.

text.p: German shares rose on Wednesday following the Dow's sharp overnight gains but once again failed to keep full pace with a U.S. rally as investors continued to show scepticism about current price levels.

The IBIS DAX index of electronic trade rose 23.77 points to 3,449.63 in early dealings, a 0.7 percent rise well short of the Dow Industrial's 2.6 percent surge following the release of favourable U.S. economic data.
Dealers noted that the short-covering in the market, particularly on Tuesday, indicated that investors thought further gains possible but little fresh money was coming in.
Traders said the next key trading level for the DAX index was 3,475 points. Once that was breached, new inflows of money into the market were expected.

Short-term, volumes were also thin due to Thursday's May-day holiday and ahead of further U.S. data, including the National Association of Purchasing Managers (NAPM) index later today and the non-farm payrolls report due on Friday.

Chemical and drugs giant Bayer topped early volumes but slid 90 pfennigs to 69.30 marks as the market was disappointed by first-quarter turnover growth, which dealers said many were expecting to be higher.

In the same sector, Schering gained 75 pfennigs to 163.70 marks after it said first-quarter group sales were up 21 percent on the year before, and that profits for the period were up between 10 and 15 percent.
